paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: a local usage ledger for tokens, cache hit rate and estimated cost per day,
per model and per workspace.
# Usage Ledger（用量账本）

A local-first usage ledger for DeepSeek Harness: mines the session logs on this
machine and reports

per-day / per-model / per-workspace token consumption,
cache hit rate, tool-vs-chat split, and an es

-model / per-workspace token consumption,
cache hit rate, tool-vs-chat split, and an estimated cost.
本地用量账本插件：从本机会话日志统计每日 / 每模型 / 每工作区的 token 消耗、缓存命中率、工具请求占比，并按配置单价估算开销。
## Install

Install it as a DeepSeek Harness plugin from this repository — in the desktop
app open the plugin ma

Or from a local clone, point the same field at the absolute path of the
checkout. The bundle patch r

egisters the `usage-ledger` entry with the ledger
dashboard in the header; no extra configuration is

the `usage-ledger` entry with the ledger
dashboard in the header; no extra configuration is needed.

When you install from a local directory by hand, keep the installed
`package.json` `name` equal to t

he specifier the profile loads (for example
`@local/usage-ledger`). The host validates that the icon

resolved through
`<specifier>/icon` stays inside a package with that exact name; a mismatch only
su

rfaces as a "Plugin metadata … icon must remain inside its package directory"
diagnostic.
## Features

- Daily token & cost overview with today / 7d / 30d / all-time range filters
- Per-model table: requ

ests, uncached input, cache read/write, output, hit rate, cost
- Share pies (tokens & cost), daily c

ost bar chart
- Workspace breakdown (sessions merged by cwd) and tool-call ranking
- **Instant start

up after the first run**: folded sessions are cached on disk, so
only logs that changed are re-read

(see Fold cache)
- **Price configuration**: a ⚙ Prices button in the header opens a per-model
price
editor (input / output / cache read / cache write, per 1M tokens)
## How pricing works

1. **Built-in catalog** — the plugin ships with USD list prices for the models
it knows (Kimi, GLM,

MiniMax, DeepSeek coding-plan models, verified against
official pricing pages). Catalog prices follo

w plugin updates.
2. **Observed models** — model names come from your own session logs, so the
edito

r always lists exactly the models you actually used.
3. **Custom overrides** — any row edited in the

⚙ dialog is persisted into your
user profile patch (via the host's config editor) and takes precede

nce over
the built-in catalog. Untouched rows keep following the catalog.
4. **Fallback** — models w

ithout any price are estimated at the `*` fallback
row (default $0.50 in / $2.00 out per 1M tokens)
and flagged in the UI.

Saving restates every historical day instantly: the plugin stores token totals
and derives cost at r

ead time, so a price edit needs neither a refold nor a
cache rewrite.
## Fold cache

A cold start replays every session log (decompressing the zstd JSONL and folding
each event), which

takes seconds once a machine has a few hundred sessions and
is repeated on every plugin activation —

including the reload that follows each
price save.

`index.js` therefore persists the fold to
`$DSH_HOME/cache/usage-ledger/fold-cache.json` (default `~

/.dsh/cache/...`,
`DSH_HOME` respected). Each entry stores the folded token/request totals plus the

session log's persistence `revision` (`dev:ino:size:mtimeNs:ctimeNs`). On
activation the plugin take

s one `sessionPersistence.list()` snapshot, adopts a
cached entry only when the revision still match

es, and re-reads just the sessions
that changed. Live sessions are always refolded from the event st

nd re-reads just the sessions
that changed. Live sessions are always refolded from the event stream.

The cache stores no cost, only measurable counters, so it is safe to delete: the
next activation sim

ply folds everything again. Writes are atomic (temp file +
rename), coalesced, and skipped when noth

ing changed; a run writes the cache
once after its startup fold and once on shutdown, so serving the

dashboard does
no extra I/O and a corrupt or partial file is ignored.

Serving is pure aggregation over the folded states: display metadata (model,
title, first prompt) is

folded from the log's own events, so opening the panel
never re-reads a session log. In particular,

titles come from `session/title`
events rather than `sessionQuery.readTitleSnapshots`, which would

reload every
session corpus on each request.
## Configuration

The plugin's config is `{ currency: string, prices: Record<string, {input,
output, cacheRead, cacheW

rite}> }`. Prefer the ⚙ dialog; hand-editing the
`usage-ledger` row of your profile's `cordis.patch.

er the ⚙ dialog; hand-editing the
`usage-ledger` row of your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` works too:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

If the host environment has no config editor, the ⚙ button is hidden and the
dashboard explains how
to edit the patch instead.
## Privacy

All data is computed locally from session logs. The HTTP endpoint listens on
the loopback interface
only and rejects cross-site requests.
## Host requirements

The ⚙ Prices editor needs a host that mounts the `configEditor` service
(DeepSeek Harness desktop an

d web both do). On hosts without it the plugin
still folds the session log and serves the dashboard

— read-only, priced from
the built-in catalog.
## Changelog

- **1.3.1** — The dashboard no longer reloads the session corpus per request:
titles are folded from

their `session/title` events (and cached) instead of
calling `sessionQuery.readTitleSnapshots`, whi

ch re-read every session log on
each GET (~8 s for 127 sessions). Serving is now pure aggregation. F

old-cache
version bumped to 2.
- **1.3.0** — Fold cache: per-session folded totals are persisted to

`$DSH_HOME/cache/usage-ledger/fold-cache.json` and invalidated by the session
log's persistence revi

sion, so activation only re-reads logs that changed
(cold start ~4.5 s on 126 sessions / 76 MB of lo

gs, warm start ~10 ms). Cost
is now derived from stored token totals at rollup time, which makes a c

ached
start bit-identical to a cold fold and lets price edits apply without a
refold. Live events th

at arrive during the first backfill are now parked
